problem: Find the saddle point of the hyperbolic paraboloid $z+2=\frac{(x+5)^{2}}{3}-\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{2}.$
worked_solution:
The general equation of a hyperbolic paraboloid with a saddle point at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ is 

$$
z-{z}_{0}=\frac{(x-{x}_{0})^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-{y}_{0})^{2}}{{b}^{2}}.
$$

To find the saddle point, we rewrite our equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}z+2 & =\frac{(x+5)^{2}}{3}-\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{2} \\ z-(-2) & =\frac{(x-(-5))^{2}}{3}-\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of a hyperbolic paraboloid with a saddle point at $(-5,2,-2).$
